final.title: Data residency is a workflow decision
final.body:
If you are rethinking data residency, start with one bounded workflow decision: where does one important data type live today, and why? For a small business, that might be customer records, invoices, or support tickets sitting in a SaaS app, email inboxes, local files, or spreadsheets. The point is not to turn this into a policy debate. It is to see whether the work is centralized enough to repeat without handholding.

That matters if you are weighing automation against another hire. AI plus workflow tools like Zapier, Make, or n8n can only connect a process when there is somewhere sensible to read from and write to. If the information is scattered across email threads and disconnected spreadsheets, the first step is usually consolidation, not automation. That is not a failure. It is just the layout you chose for convenience or cost.

For the kind of owner-operator Bareni is built for, this often looks like a trade-off made earlier: the inbox became the system because it was already there, or the spreadsheet became the process because it was easy to start. If you have tried ChatGPT but have not tied AI to a real workflow, this is usually the place to look first.

A practical next step: pick one recurring workflow and map where the data actually lives at each step. Then ask yourself, in plain English: if I wanted to automate this, could a tool like Zapier or Make read and write where the data currently lives, or would I need to move it first?
